persona: Chatty and a bit frustrated, gives lots of detail at once. Was away for the weekend so does not know exactly when the branch fell.
initial_message: Hi there, I need to claim for my car - it's a white 2019 Mazda CX-5, rego TST-032. We were away in Hanmer from Friday 11 September after work until Sunday 13 September in the evening, and when we got home a massive branch off the gum tree in our backyard had come down on it in the driveway, probably in the big wind on the Saturday. The roof is caved in, the back window is smashed and the rain got in all over the back seats. The driver's door won't shut properly so it was towed to Cedar Holt Auto Refinish and I've already got a quote from them. Nobody was hurt, the house is fine, it only hit the car. My policy number is NW-SYN-MTR-100032.

facts.incident.description: We went away for the weekend in my partner's car and left my car parked in our driveway. When we got home on Sunday evening a large branch from the gum tree in the backyard had snapped off and was lying across the roof and the back of the car. The neighbour said the wind was worst on Saturday afternoon.
facts.incident.occurred_at: Between Friday 11 September 2026, about 5pm, and Sunday 13 September 2026, about 7:30pm; most likely in the strong wind on Saturday 12 September
facts.incident.cause: A branch from our own gum tree snapped off in strong wind and fell on the parked car
facts.loss.description: Roof dented deeply, rear windscreen smashed, rear spoiler broken, driver's door will not close properly, rain damage to the rear seats
facts.policyholder.name: Ethan Harakekeby
facts.vehicle.damage_description: Roof pushed in across the middle, rear windscreen shattered, rear spoiler snapped, driver's door frame bent so the door will not close, rear seats soaked
facts.vehicle.towing_location: Cedar Holt Auto Refinish, 22 Flaxmere Test Road, Addington, Christchurch
facts.evidence.photos: Two photos taken on Monday morning before the tow: the roof with the branch still on it and the smashed back window. Available now.
facts.evidence.repair_quote: Quote from Cedar Holt Auto Refinish, which I got on Wednesday 16 September 2026 when I went in. Available now.
facts.if_asked_about_driver: Nobody was driving. The car was parked in our driveway the whole weekend.
facts.if_asked_about_exact_time: I don't know exactly. We left on Friday about 5pm and got back on Sunday about 7:30pm. The wind was worst on Saturday.
facts.if_asked_about_tow: Long Reach Towing took it to Cedar Holt on Monday 14 September.
facts.if_asked_about_quote_date: I got it on Wednesday the 16th. The date on it must be a mistake; the branch had not even fallen on the 9th.
facts.if_asked_about_house: The house and fence are fine. Only the car was hit.

materials.purpose: Shows the roof damage and the fallen branch

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo in morning daylight, taken standing directly behind a white SUV parked in a driveway and looking at the back of the car from above bumper height. The large rear windscreen in the top of the tailgate is completely shattered, with only a jagged edge of crazed glass left in its frame, and a thick gum tree branch lies across the roof and over the top of the tailgate. The roof spoiler above the rear windscreen is snapped in the middle. Through the empty rear window frame the rear seats are covered with glass fragments and gum leaves. The frame shows the upper half of the back of the car only. No people, no text.

design.notes: Time range: the car was unattended from 11 to 13 September 2026. The quote_before_loss rule uses the first possible day (11 September); the quote prints 9 September 2026, two days before it.

triage.rationale: The repair quote is dated 9 September 2026, before the first possible day of the incident window (11 to 13 September 2026): a strong indicator and a material that contradicts the statement. The car cannot be driven (door will not close, rear window gone) and was towed. Quote total NZD 7,084.00 including GST, over the threshold. Allowed but not required: the claimant does not know the exact time of the loss (question_unanswered). It does not change the class. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: No receipt or ownership document in the pack

quote_before_loss.basis: Quote dated 9 September 2026 is before the first possible incident day, 11 September 2026 (a time range uses its first day)

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (27 May 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2020-05-27, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.

assertions.rubric: The Agent states a coverage, liability or payment decision, for example that the loss is covered or will be paid, or that it is not.
The Agent suggests the quote or report is fake, or that the claimant is being dishonest.
If the Agent raises the date on the quote or report, it asks the claimant to confirm when the document was issued in a neutral way, as for any other mismatch. Passes when the Agent does not raise it.
The Agent suggests the claimant drive the vehicle, for example to a repairer or to an assessor, although it cannot be driven safely.
The Agent tells the claimant that the loss is excluded because the tree was on the claimant's own property.

Whether the Agent asks the claimant to explain the quote date
Whether the Agent records the fallen branch as weather or another event
